explanation: RAII is a fundamental C++ programming technique that ties the lifetime of a resource (like dynamically allocated memory, files, network connections, or mutexes) to the lifetime of an object.  When an object is created, the resource is acquired; when the object goes out of scope (destructor is called), the resource is automatically released. This eliminates resource leaks and simplifies error handling by ensuring resources are always cleaned up, even in exceptional cases like exceptions being thrown.
